functions: Cuts what belongs to the mechanism from what does not. Without it no quantity has a frame of reference, and nothing else is definable.
What enters, accumulates and leaves. This is where delay lives — a mechanism with nothing accumulating answers instantly and needs no steering.
The rules that set rates, and the settings you can move. Without it the mechanism has no behaviour to explain and no handle to act on.
Reading the result, comparing it to the target, and deciding when to act. This is the function a chain lacks, and the only one bound by two physical laws.
Which values are measured, borrowed or guessed. Without it the model cannot tell a fact from a hunch, and defends both with the same confidence.

organs.name: Boundary
rules: Draw the boundary around a complete loop, never around a team.
If the slowest stock's turnover exceeds the fastest by more than five times, split into two mechanisms.
A valid boundary is crossed by a finite number of named flows.
Write events, not objects. « The call is booked », not « sales ».
Several starts or several ends are normal. Every end event must map to an output in organ 10.
organs.why: It decides what you model and what you treat as outside. The most structural choice there is: a badly drawn boundary cuts a loop in half, and you then observe a cause without its feedback.
organs.how: List the events that bring something into the mechanism and those that take it out. There can be several on each side — a lead can leave because it closed or because it died, and those are two distinct ends. Then check that the main loop closes inside.

organs.name: Declared objective
rules: A value, a unit, a horizon. None of the three is optional.
The unit must read directly off organ 10. A target on a middle step means you pilot a proxy.
Set the acceptable minimum at the same time as the target. Without a written floor, any gap becomes negotiable after the fact.
One target per mechanism. Two competing targets mean either two mechanisms or an unmade trade-off.
organs.why: It provides the term of comparison without which no gap exists — and without a gap, nothing in the whole mechanism triggers a decision.
organs.how: A metric, a target value, a unit, a horizon, and a floor. The metric must read directly off the outputs, not off an intermediate step.

organs.name: Revealed objective

cols.l: What was dropped first under pressure

rules: Filled by retrospective observation only, never by declaration.
Look at the incentives, not the speeches: what is measured, what is paid, what is publicly celebrated.
One observation per constraint squeeze. Three pressure spikes in six months give three independent readings.
If it matches the declared one, write it anyway. Alignment is information, not its absence.
organs.why: It names what the mechanism optimises in practice, which is not always what it announces. The distance between the two shows up in no variable: only in behaviour under pressure.
organs.how: Recall the last time pressure rose. Note what was dropped first. That is the real objective function.

organs.name: Constraints
rules: Pick the nature first: it decides how the next four fields read and which alert applies.
A throughput recharges and degrades gradually. A threshold recharges and blocks flat. A depleting stock never refills. A presence is there or it is not.
Express it in the unit of the flow it limits, not in a management unit. « 60 calls a week », not « 2 full-time equivalents ».
For a depleting stock, the limit is an absolute volume and the load a per-period draw: runway is the ratio of the two.
If a limit lifts through an internal decision, it is not a constraint but a frozen parameter. It belongs to organ 12.
organs.why: They bound what is reachable, hence which iterations are worth attempting. But they do not all behave the same way as you approach them, and that behaviour decides how to watch them.
organs.how: Pick the nature first, it changes the meaning of the following fields. A throughput recharges and degrades gradually: the alert is utilisation. A threshold blocks flat without warning: the alert is remaining margin. A depleting stock never refills: the alert is runway, the limit divided by the per-period draw. A presence is indivisible: the alert is replacement time.

organs.name: Owner

cols.l: Can hold a refusal against the founder?

rules: One physical person per lever. A role, a function or a team does not satisfy the rule.
Write the authority, not the accountability, always in the same form: « X may change Y without asking anyone. »
A lever with no named owner is not a lever. It drops back into constraints until someone picks it up.
Validate with the refusal test. If the answer is no, the authority is fictional.
organs.why: It names who can move the levers and refuse a passage. Without it, rules become recommendations that get bypassed the moment someone is in a hurry.
organs.how: A physical person, never a role. Write what they may change without asking anyone, then answer the refusal test.

organs.name: Inputs
rules: Three values per input: volume, variability, source. Volume alone allows no attribution.
If the input comes from another mechanism, write its name. The link becomes an interface to watch.
An input is transformed and comes back out; a resource is consumed without coming out. Resources go to the register.
Every input must be received by a named flow.
organs.why: They describe what arrives from outside without you steering it. Without them, a variation coming from upstream looks exactly like a drop in internal performance.
organs.how: Three values per input: volume, variability, source. If the input comes from another mechanism, write its name.

organs.name: Disturbances
rules: List the known sources before trying to measure anything. The list alone is usable.
A disturbance that is both severe and observable must become a modelled input.
A recurring, predictable disturbance is not one: it is an unmodelled input. Move it up to organ 06.
Above thirty per cent unexplained variance, stop iterating and fix the model.
organs.why: They capture the share of variation your model does not explain. Their size measures the quality of your model, not the chaos of the world.
organs.how: List the known sources, then note their severity and whether they are observable. One that is both severe and observable should become an input.

organs.name: Stocks
rules: Two mandatory values: level and turnover time.
Measure turnover with the freeze test: if you cut all inflow now, how long until it empties?
One stock per kind of content, not per process step. Two steps accumulating the same thing are one stock.
Actively hunt the invisible stocks: queues, pending decisions, unwritten knowledge.
organs.why: They are the mechanism's memory and the reason it does not react instantly. The most systematically forgotten organ, and the one whose absence costs the most.
organs.how: Two values: level and turnover. For turnover, ask how long the stock would take to empty if you cut all inflow right now.

organs.name: Flows
rules: Every flow names its source stock and its destination stock. One of the two may be the outside, never both.
Always express units per unit of time, never as a percentage. A percentage has no time dimension.
Check as you write, not afterwards: inflows minus outflows equals the change in stock.
A flow touching no stock is a step. Rename it or delete it.
organs.why: They give the mechanism its dynamics. Without them you know where it stands, not where it is going — and a swelling stock goes unnoticed until it overflows.
organs.how: Each flow names its origin and destination; one of the two may be the outside. Express in units per unit of time, never as a percentage.

organs.name: Outputs
rules: Write the outputs before the inputs. Always. Starting with inputs models what is available rather than what matters.
Every unit that enters must show up in an output or in a stock. Do the arithmetic before moving on.
For each output, name its destination. An output with no destination signals a badly drawn boundary.
Find the induced outputs with one question: what does this mechanism impose on whoever comes next?
organs.why: They count everything that leaves, including what nobody wanted. Uncounted outputs are exactly the costs the mechanism dumps on its neighbours.
organs.how: The wanted outputs first, with their destination. Then hunt the induced ones by asking what this mechanism imposes on whoever comes next.

organs.name: Levers
rules: Three cumulative conditions: adjustable now, by a named person, without outside approval.
Write a setting, never an improvement. « Length of the confirmation sequence », not « better confirmation ».
Each lever points at a precise relation in organ 13. A lever with no point of action is a wish.
Cap yourself at five levers. Beyond that you describe the space of possibilities, not of decisions.
organs.why: They make the model actionable rather than descriptive. Without levers you can understand a mechanism perfectly and never be able to move it.
organs.how: Write a setting, never an improvement. Each lever points at a precise rule and carries its owner's name. Five at most.

organs.name: Frozen parameters
rules: Two mandatory fields: reason for freezing, unfreezing condition. Without the second it is a constraint in disguise.
The condition must be observable by an existing sensor. « If it becomes a problem » is not a condition.
Set a review date on every freeze. A freeze with no review date turns into a belief.
Anything that is neither lever nor constraint is a frozen parameter. There is no fourth bucket.
organs.why: They make explicit what you chose not to touch. Without that, the question reopens at every difficult discussion and the argument has to be rebuilt from scratch.
organs.how: For each one: the reason for the freeze, and the unfreezing condition. The condition must be observable by a sensor that already exists.

organs.name: Transformation rules

cols.l: Relation (write the relation, not the result)

rules: Write the relation, never the result. « Close rate drops beyond 48 calls », not « close rate is 24 % ».
Look for at least one non-linearity per mechanism. If you find none, you have not looked at the extremes of the range.
For each relation, note whether it serves to predict or to intervene. Only the latter justifies an iteration.
A rule linking more than three variables is almost always several badly separated rules.
organs.why: They link inputs and levers to outputs. This is what makes prediction possible, hence choosing between several iterations before launching them.
organs.how: Write the relation, not the result. Flag the non-linear ones: a model with no threshold never surprises you, it only returns what you put in.

organs.name: Delays
rules: Add the three terms: process delay, turnover of the stocks crossed, sensor latency. Forgetting the third is the most common mistake.
Measure end to end, from setting the lever to reading the result — not to the real effect, which you cannot see.
Express the delay in the same unit as the cadence, otherwise the comparison that protects from over-steering is impossible.
If several paths exist between action and effect, keep the longest. That one bounds the cadence.
organs.why: They measure the time between an action and its readable effect. This is what sets how fast you are allowed to steer without making the mechanism oscillate.
organs.how: Add the process delay and the sensor latency. That sum bounds the decision cadence, and the second term is the one always forgotten.

organs.name: Sensors
rules: Three mandatory attributes: latency, noise amplitude, incentive created. Two out of three is not enough.
Measure the noise over a period without intervention, otherwise you measure your own corrections.
Name who produces the data. If it is the person being evaluated on it, write that down: the incentive is part of the sensor.
One sensor per measured output. A sensor measuring three things measures none of them properly.
organs.why: They produce the picture of reality you decide on. You never decide on reality, always on its measurement — which has its own latency and its own noise.
organs.how: Three mandatory attributes: latency, noise, and who enters the data. Measure the noise over a period without intervention, otherwise you measure your own corrections.

organs.name: Gap
rules: Same unit, same window, same scope as the target. All three conditions.
A gap is always written with the sensor noise. « +4, noise ±9 » reads correctly; « +4 » reads false.
One aggregation window per mechanism, fixed in advance. Changing it based on the result is the first step into self-deception.
Write the signed gap, never the absolute value. The direction carries most of the information.
organs.why: It is the only place in the mechanism that triggers a decision. Every other organ describes or transforms; this one fires.
organs.how: Enter the current measurement and the aggregation window. The target comes from organ 02 and the gap computes itself. Always compare it to the sensor noise.

organs.name: Policy

cols.l: What happens inside the dead band

rules: Cadence greater than or equal to total delay. Non-negotiable: the only rule here that admits no exception.
Dead band strictly greater than sensor noise over the chosen window. Below that, you react to your own noise.
One lever per cycle. Two simultaneous levers make attribution impossible.
Write the inaction explicitly. Otherwise someone will act.
organs.why: It turns a gap into action, with three settings: cadence, dead band, gain. Without it, the intensity of the reaction depends on who is looking that day.
organs.how: Cadence must be greater than or equal to the total delay. The dead band must exceed sensor noise. One lever adjusted per cycle.

organs.name: Loops
rules: Write each loop as a closed cycle of three to five links. Beyond that it is probably wrong or badly cut.
Qualify every loop: balancing or reinforcing. An unqualified loop is drawn, not modelled.
Note each loop's delay. Two loops at different speeds produce a two-stage behaviour nobody understands without this.
Note which one dominates in the current regime, and under what condition dominance flips.
organs.why: They describe the paths by which an effect comes back onto its own cause. Without a reinforcing loop nothing grows; without a balancing one everything explodes.
organs.how: Three to five links per loop, its type, and its delay. If no loop closes inside, it is the boundary that is badly drawn.

organs.name: Evidence level
rules: Three levels only. No middle ground — nuance is always used to dodge.
Every value carries its date. A measurement has a shelf life, past which it changes level.
Set the shelf life per type of value, once, before filling anything in.
A value tagged « hunch » that carries a structural conclusion is a friction, not an imprecision.
organs.why: It tags where every value comes from. This is what stops a number being relitigated forever: a value marked « hunch » is discussed once, then becomes an iteration.
organs.how: Three levels only — measured, benchmark, hunch — with the date. A six-month-old measurement is no longer a measurement, it has become a historical benchmark.

organs.name: Structural assumptions

cols.l: Falsifiable claim (« X does not depend on Y »)

rules: Write each assumption as a falsifiable claim. One you cannot contradict is not an assumption.
Look in the four usual places: independence, linearity, sequentiality, stationarity.
For each assumption, note the test that would invalidate it. Without it, it stays an assumption forever.
A structural assumption untested after six months becomes a priority iteration, whatever its score.
organs.why: They record what you assumed about the shape of the relations, not about their values. A value error corrects itself through iteration; a shape error never does.
organs.how: Write each assumption as a falsifiable claim, of the form « X does not depend on Y », with the test that would invalidate it.

organs.name: Excluded scope
rules: Every exclusion carries two fields: the reason, and an observable re-entry signal.
The signal must be measurable by a sensor that already exists. One requiring new instrumentation will never fire.
Separate excluded by choice from excluded by ignorance. The second is a debt to settle.
Re-read the excluded scope at every boundary revision. The two organs move together or not at all.
organs.why: It separates what was ruled out from what was forgotten. Without it, nobody can tell whether a missing element was examined or never considered.
organs.how: For each exclusion: the reason, and the signal that would force it back in. The signal must be measurable with the sensors you already have.

frictions.name: Conservation broken
frictions.t: 10 units appear with no origin. A stock or an output is missing from the model. Go back to the boundary before hunting in the stocks.

frictions.name: Cadence law broken
frictions.t: You correct every 1 day a mechanism that takes 7 days to answer. Every correction leaves before the previous one has produced its effect: oscillation is guaranteed.

frictions.name: Dead band law broken
frictions.t: Your decision rule fires on gaps smaller than the noise of your own measurement. You are reacting to your instrument, not to your mechanism. The dead band must exceed the noise — that is an inequality, not a comfort setting.

frictions.name: Blind gap
frictions.t: The observed gap is smaller than the sensor noise. It means nothing. Widen the aggregation window or reduce the noise before interpreting anything.

frictions.name: Clock mismatch
frictions.t: The fast stock sees the slow one as a constant, the slow one sees the fast one as noise. A single cadence over-steers one and under-reacts to the other. Split into two mechanisms.

frictions.name: Throughput saturated
frictions.t: Sales rep capacity runs at 97 % of its limit, past the point where degradation starts. Waiting time grows non-linearly: any upstream volume gain is absorbed by the queue before it reaches the result.

frictions.name: Runway too short
frictions.t: Cash does not refill. At the current draw of 38000 € per period, 3.2 periods remain. Utilisation means nothing here: what counts is the depletion rate.

frictions.name: Single point of failure
frictions.t: Senior sales rep is an indivisible resource: it does not degrade gradually, it disappears at once. Replacing it takes 90 days, and the mechanism must run without it for that long.

frictions.name: Structural hunch
frictions.c: Sales rep capacity · evidence level: hunch
frictions.t: A constraint bounds the space of viable iterations. If it rests on an untested hunch, you may be ruling out iterations because of an imaginary limit. Verify before iterating.

frictions.name: Revealed objective unknown
frictions.t: Until the sacrifice test is done, you steer towards a target without knowing whether the mechanism pursues another one. This is where the most expensive pathologies live.
